source_global_assumptions.content: The candidate class X={L_1,L_2,...} is countable and known to the algorithm through its description; every candidate is infinite. A hidden target K belongs to X. The adversary reveals one target string per time step and must eventually enumerate all of K. The current results use full enumeration; partial enumeration is mentioned as prior work, not the present default.

If S_t is the set of adversarial strings through t, generation in the limit means there exists a finite t* such that o_t belongs to K minus S_t for every t>=t*. The introduction only writes freshness against the adversary prefix. The algorithms use the stronger available convention: used by neither adversary nor generator. An adversary can reveal a point already generated, but the finite game explicitly disallows the adversary repeating itself. O is the set of generated target strings (or all generated strings intersected with K inside every density); multiplicity does not contribute.

The author explicitly calls the results information theoretic, allowing access to the countable class description and disclaiming efficient finite-sample or polynomial-time procedures. No membership-decision algorithm, computable rank/tree, effective presentation of all candidates, or finite running-time bound is supplied as a standing theorem hypothesis. The text says a countable discrete universe admits an effective enumeration; this is an author normalization assertion, not a uniform effectiveness theorem for arbitrary language classes. In higher dimensions the detailed reduction assumes discrete coordinate-value sets; coordinatewise normalization preserves incidences with axis-parallel windows.

For A subset of positive naturals, delta_f(A,N)=liminf_(k→infinity) min_(1<=m<=f(k)) |A intersect [m,m+k-1]|/k, with nondecreasing f:N→N union {infinity}. At f=infinity the inner minimum/infimum ranges over all positive starts and gives lower Banach density. Density in K is read in the increasing order of K, equivalently |O intersect K intersect I|/|K intersect I| as |K intersect I|→infinity over coordinate intervals I. Relative intervals [a,b]_K use positions in the ordered target, not coordinate differences. In d dimensions ordinary density ranges over all bounded axis-parallel rectangles R with |R intersect K|→infinity.

On X the basis is U_(L,F)={Lprime in X: F subseteq Lprime subseteq L}, for L in X and finite F in the countable universe. The source calls this topology Hausdorff and first countable. Derived sets are computed relative to X: X^(0)=X, X^(i+1)=d(X^(i)); the class rank is the least ordinal with empty derivative, infinity if none. Finite-rank results use a finite r. This is the containment-refined topology; Remark 1 distinguishes the coarser finite-evidence topology without the upper containment condition. The numerical point-rank convention on printed p.35 is internally inconsistent by one; strict rank comparisons and finite class rank are recorded without silently choosing one indexing.

For a fixed nondecreasing divergent g:[0,infinity)→[0,infinity), filtered density retains rectangles along which |R intersect K|/[g(Vol(R)) log Vol(R)]→infinity. The detailed theorem fixes g (named f there) before choosing its algorithm. Vol is geometric/discrete scale as used by the source, and the proof uses L(R)<=Vol(R)<=L(R)^d. Exact conventions for zero-volume, side-length-one and empty admissible families are not specified. The overview instead describes a sequence as nondegenerate if there exists some divergent function witnessing that ratio; that quantifier is kept separate from the fixed-function detailed theorem.

lean_statement_reconstruction: Let X be any set of languages, sequence : Nat → Point X, terminal K : Point X, and R,r : Nat. If the R-th internal derivative D_R of X is empty, K lies in D_r \ D_(r+1), every sequence term is a proper subset of K, and each u∈K belongs to all sufficiently late sequence terms, then there is N such that for every n≥N there is q<r with sequence(n)∈D_q \ D_(q+1). The derivative starts at all points and repeatedly retains a point of the current set exactly when every finite positive neighborhood below it contains another point of the current set.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: ∀ {X} {sequence : Nat→Point X} {K : Point X} {R r : Nat}, [D_R=∅] → [K∈D_r ∧ K∉D_(r+1)] → [(∀n,sequence(n).val⊊K.val) ∧ (∀u∈K.val ∃N_u ∀n≥N_u,u∈sequence(n).val)] → ∃N ∀n≥N ∃q : Nat, q<r ∧ sequence(n)∈D_q\D_(q+1). N can depend on all preceding data and hypotheses; q can additionally depend on n.
comparison_summary: The target states the intended eventual rank drop for a genuinely approaching proper-subset sequence in a finite-rank class. It does not formalize the unqualified literal source sentence for arbitrary sequences merely having K as a cluster point or containing K infinitely often.

component_comparisons.detail: Requires every sequence term to be a proper subset and every terminal element to be eventually permanently present; yields ∃N ∀n>=N ∃q<r exactRank(sequence n,q).
The broader native version accepts eventual membership in every finite-evidence neighborhood and explicit ∀n,sequence n≠K.

Without a global empty-derivative premise, an exact-rank terminal plus genuine basis convergence implies eventual nonmembership in D_r. Global finite rank is used by the fuller endpoint to produce a finite exact q.

strength_assessment: The Lean target strengthens sequence hypotheses to all terms being proper subsets plus pointwise eventual coverage. Native claim_4_11 separately handles basis convergence with explicit terminal exclusion. These are qualifications of an ambiguous/overbroad source statement, while arbitrary X generalizes its class domain. Both conclude one eventual threshold N and a possibly n-dependent q<r; no monotone rank decrease along time is added.
algorithm_scope: Semantic eventual rank comparison only. N and q are existentially quantified and need not be computable; no learner, rank oracle, convergence rate or named witness selector appears.
same_witness_and_interface_assembly: N may depend on X, sequence, terminal and rank data; q may also depend on n. There is no single eventual q or computable modulus.
discrepancies: The source says K is the limit point of a sequence; its proof assumes convergence and genuine accumulation. Lean requires explicit convergence data and properness/exclusion. A constant sequence J_n=K makes the unqualified literal strict-drop statement fail; this is a source-qualification issue, not evidence of a Lean bug.
Lean uses exact zero-based levels D_r minus D_(r+1), consistent with the source proof on printed p.38. The source rank assignment on printed p.35 also gives a conflicting one-based description.

Lean’s derivative is internal: a retained point must already lie in the previous derivative. Source ambient derived sets agree through finite iterations from the whole Hausdorff space because those iterated sets are closed, but there is no blanket equality of these two operators on arbitrary nonclosed subsets.
suspected_source_issues: Literal limit point of a sequence can mean a cluster point, but the proof assumes convergence and says a selected subsequence still converges.
Allowing J_j=K infinitely often defeats a strict eventual inequality; the printed statement does not explicitly exclude this.

Printed p.35 assigns rank i to X^(i-1) minus X^(i) but then assigns rank 0 to X minus X^(1); printed p.38 instead uses rank>=alpha iff membership in X^(alpha). These conventions must not be silently merged.
limitations: The source’s literal cluster-point reading is not covered.
A source terminal of rank zero cannot admit the full proper convergent hypotheses; the Lean conclusion q<0 is correspondingly impossible.
